meta.scope: Venezuela batch 3 — Major states/regions (Zulia, Miranda, Bolívar, Carabobo), health-system stress, fiscal/oil-revenue architecture, and debt. Continues under data-quality caution.

candidates.title: Estado Zulia — western oil and population pole
candidates.description: Western state centred on Maracaibo. Largest state population mass and a major oil-producing region. High service and living-condition stress in independent surveys.
candidates.notes: Demographic and oil-geography node. Continuously appears among the highest-stress states in independent living-conditions diagnostics; large absolute population affected by service failures and poverty.

candidates.title: Estado Miranda — capital-region periphery
candidates.description: State surrounding and interwoven with the Caracas metro. Large population, mixed urban conditions, and high absolute poverty and service-stress counts.
candidates.notes: Completes the greater Caracas statistical geography. Frequently ranked among the largest absolute poverty and service-deprivation masses.

candidates.title: Estado Bolívar — southern mining and industrial
candidates.description: Southern state with major mining (iron, gold, etc.) and industrial activity (Ciudad Guayana). Distinct resource and living-conditions profile.
candidates.notes: Mining and heavy-industry geography. Independent diagnostics show elevated multidimensional stress; resource extraction coexists with severe service and income gaps.

candidates.title: Estado Carabobo — central industrial corridor
candidates.description: Central state with significant industrial and commercial activity (Valencia area). Intermediate-to-high living-condition stress.
candidates.notes: Industrial-corridor node. Completes the set of major population and economic poles outside the pure oil west and the capital.

candidates.title: Sistema de salud — acceso y deficiencias
candidates.description: Public health-system access and reported deficiencies in infrastructure, personnel, medicines, equipment and basic services (water, electricity) at care points.
candidates.notes: Lived health-system stress. Large majority rely on public facilities; independent diagnostics report widespread shortages of medicines, supplies, equipment and basic services inside those facilities. Private care is largely inaccessible by cost.

candidates.title: Ingresos petroleros del Estado
candidates.description: Fiscal and external revenues derived from oil exports. Primary financing source of the public sector and of foreign-exchange supply.
candidates.notes: Core fiscal-revenue node. Recovery of production and commercialisation arrangements (including licensed private operators) directly shapes the government’s foreign-exchange and budget capacity. Transparency of flows remains limited.

candidates.title: Deuda pública / Public and PDVSA debt
candidates.description: Stock of public and PDVSA external debt. Subject of restructuring efforts; official stock series have not been regularly published for years.
candidates.notes: Critical sustainability node under extreme opacity. Independent estimates place the combined public + PDVSA external debt in the low-to-mid hundreds of billions of USD — a multiple of GDP. Restructuring is on the policy agenda.

candidates.title: SENIAT — tax administration
candidates.description: National tax authority. Publishes residual tax-collection statistics that form the non-oil revenue side of the budget.
candidates.notes: Non-oil revenue node. Tax collection exists and is reported in residual form, but oil remains the dominant fiscal resource; the overall budget framework is characterised by limited transparency.

candidates.title: Estado Anzoátegui — eastern oil and industrial
candidates.description: Eastern state with significant oil and industrial activity. Intermediate-to-high living-condition stress in independent diagnostics.
candidates.notes: Eastern oil/industrial geography. Completes the set of major hydrocarbon and population states.

candidates.title: HumVenezuela — independent living-conditions diagnostics
candidates.description: Independent multi-source diagnostic platform that compiles and publishes state-level indicators of humanitarian and living-condition stress (services, health, food, etc.).
candidates.notes: Complementary independent source to ENCOVI. Frequently cited for state-level service and health-system deficiency rates; helps fill geographic detail that official statistics do not provide.

proposed_edges.basis: Zulia is a primary geographic domain in independent household and living-conditions surveys.
Miranda forms the principal demographic and economic periphery of the greater Caracas region.
Health-access and perception indicators are drawn from ENCOVI and complementary independent diagnostics.
Oil-revenue flows are directly tied to production volumes and commercialisation arrangements.
PDVSA debt is a large component of the overall public-sector external-debt stock.
Tax collection is the main non-oil revenue complement to hydrocarbon income.
HumVenezuela diagnostics provide state-level detail on service and health-system deficiencies.
